tagline: We make a number for every game. We bet the ones where the market's wrong.

games.market: Rays -132 / Guardians +112 (FanDuel), total 6.5; run line Rays -1.5 (+135)
games.matchup: Tampa Bay Rays @ Cleveland Guardians — ALCS Game 5, series tied 2-2
games.our_fair: Tampa Bay 55.0% / Cleveland 45.0% (devigged FanDuel — Pinnacle has no market listed for this game)
games.take: Rays took Game 4, 7-3, to tie the series, and the market has them as the clear Game 5 favorite. Drew Rasmussen (1.29 postseason ERA) has been the Rays' best arm all October; Cleveland counters with Parker Messick, 0-2 with a 3.09 ERA this postseason. The market's 55/45 split looks priced right — Rasmussen's edge is real but Messick is no pushover and Cleveland's pen has been the series' best weapon. No true edge at -132, but the lean is the better starting pitcher with the sharper recent form.
games.title: ALCS Game 5
games.weather: All-clear: sunny, high 61°F, south wind ~9 mph, 0% precipitation. No NWS alerts in effect.

games.take: Sunday night is as close to a coin flip as the market makes them — our number says the same. Green Bay opened -3 and got bet down to -1.5, and Dallas's defense is carrying a long injury list into Lambeau. Both offenses can score (53.5 is the week's highest total), but Dallas's banged-up defense is the one concrete mismatch. No true edge here; the lean is the home team with the healthier defense in a pick'em.
games.title: SNF: Cowboys @ Packers
games.weather: All-clear: no NWS watches/warnings/advisories for Green Bay; reported perfect conditions.

games.matchup: Los Angeles Chargers @ Kansas City Chiefs
games.take: Kansas City is 4-0 against a winless Chargers team, and the market is charging you for it: 80% implied on the Chiefs. The Chiefs are the better team, full stop — but 7.5 points is a heavy lay in a divisional game with a 41.5 total, and the line has already slid from -8.5. No true edge here; the lean is the divisional underdog catching more than a touchdown.
games.title: Chargers @ Chiefs
games.weather: All-clear: no NWS watches/warnings/advisories for Kansas City.

games.take: The week's wildest flip: Philadelphia opened -1.5 and the market swung all the way to Carolina -3. When a line moves 4.5 points, the market is telling you something changed — but you're now laying the worst of it. Our number agrees with Carolina as the better team, just not at this price. No true edge here; the lean is the home team getting a field goal in a game the market chased.
games.title: Panthers @ Eagles
games.weather: All-clear: no NWS watches/warnings/advisories for Philadelphia.

games.take: Caleb Williams is expected back after missing three games, and Michael Penix Jr. is full-go for Atlanta — both offenses at full strength under a dome roof. The total climbed from 49.5 to 52.5 and the spread tightened to -1.5 as Williams' return got priced in. Our number has it a coin flip, same as the market. No true edge here; the lean is the road favorite with its QB1 back in a dome shootout setup.
games.title: Bears @ Falcons
games.weather: Dome/retractable roof; no NWS alerts in effect.

games.take: Baker Mayfield misses his third straight game and rookie Jalon Daniels starts for Tampa — yet the line moved TOWARD the Bucs (+3 to +2.5) while over 70% of public bets landed on Pittsburgh. When the books move against the crowd, they're telling you the rookie is live. Our number still has Pittsburgh, but the market's respect for Daniels is the real signal here. No true edge; the lean is the home underdog the books won't let drift.
games.title: Steelers @ Buccaneers

games.take: Buffalo opened -6 and got bet down to -5.5/-4.5 — the market keeps shading toward the home Raiders all week. Buffalo is the better team and our number agrees, but 53.5 is a monster total in a dome and the Raiders have been a live underdog all season. No true edge here; the lean is the home team catching points in a game the market keeps drifting toward.
games.title: Bills @ Raiders
games.weather: Dome; no NWS alerts in effect.

games.take: Lamar Jackson is officially OUT (ankle) and Tyler Huntley starts his second straight game — the market dropped Baltimore from -5.5 to -3 on the news. Huntley has won his last three starts averaging 33.7 points, so this isn't the usual backup-QB discount, and Cleveland's defense is missing pieces inside. Our number has Baltimore, but the market already did the Jackson adjustment. No true edge here; the lean is the home divisional dog catching a field goal against a backup QB.
